- **Date:** 2026-11-03
- **Commit:** b72f0f32310d (uncommitted changes)
- **Corpus:** 25 documents, 170 chunks, fingerprint `398b2f2aac8822d0`
- **Questions:** 50 (`tests/copilot_eval/questions.yaml`, version 1): 24 in-corpus, 10 out-of-corpus, 9 adversarial, 7 other-intent
- **Provider chain used:** no language model for the retrieval and end-to-end sections (rule-based); scripted fake providers `evala`, `evalb`, `evalc` (`eval-fake-model`) for the rephrase and failover sections.

- **Retrieval floors in force:** score >= 6.5, coverage >= 0.4

## Gates

| Gate | Value | Target | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| hit@3 served (in-corpus, retrieval) | 0.875 | >= 0.85 | PASS |
| correct refusal (out-of-corpus, end to end) | 0.800 | >= 0.90 | FAIL |
| accepted answers with an unknown number | 0 | <= 0 | PASS |
| adversarial cases handled | 1.000 | >= 1.00 | PASS |

CP-12 (hybrid embeddings) rule from the roadmap: unlocked only if the hit@3 gate fails after tuning. Here it **passes** in-sample, so CP-12 is **skipped** by that rule. Read the out-of-sample estimate below before relying on that: it is lower.

**What a user gets is lower than the retrieval gate suggests.** Only 10 of 24 in-corpus questions reach retrieval at all (the rest carry no docs cue and are routed to an older intent, by CP-7's design), so the end-to-end cited-answer rate is 10/24 = 0.417. The retrieval gate measures the retriever, not that.

These are small-sample numbers. One in-corpus question is worth 4.2 points of hit@3 and one out-of-corpus question is worth 10 points of refusal. The questions were written by the author of the system.

## Retrieval

Ranking quality with no floors (does the right chunk come out on top?), 24 in-corpus questions: hit@1 **0.708**, hit@3 **0.875**, hit@5 0.917, MRR 0.793. Routing cues are ignored here; this is the retriever alone.

What the product actually shows depends on two floors (score and coverage). Operating points, same questions:

| Operating point | Score floor | Coverage floor | hit@3 served | Correct refusal | Out-of-sample (leave-one-out) hit / refusal |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| CP-6 placeholder | 6.0 | none | 0.875 | 0.700 | not fitted |
| Best score floor alone | 8 | none | 0.833 | 0.900 | 0.792 / 0.800 |
| **Best score and coverage floors (fitted here)** | 6.5 | 0.45 | 0.875 | 0.900 | 0.833 / 0.700 |
| **Product defaults now** | 6.5 | 0.4 | 0.875 | 0.900 | n/a |

The fit picks the middle of the plateau of equally good points (6 grid points tied). The in-sample figures are flattered because every question was visible when the floors were chosen; the leave-one-out column refits without each question and scores only that question, which is the honest estimate. Questions wrong out-of-sample: D11, D13, D16, D23, O01, O04, O10.

Retrieval misses at the product defaults:

- **D13** (not served): "What does the physics v2 model not model?"; expected chunk ranks 8 with no floors
- **D16** (not served): "What does the sensitivity study not show?"; expected chunk ranks 4 with no floors; top served: docs/SENSITIVITY.md > Physics sensitivity (Task 10) > Study 1: physics 1, production rule
- **D23** (not served): "What can the Copilot not do?"; expected chunk not in the top 20

Reading the in-corpus misses: the question says "Copilot" where the document says "assistant", and "not model" against the heading "Not modelled", which plain keyword matching cannot bridge; a near-miss (expected chunk at rank 4) is a ranking problem instead. Embeddings (CP-12) could help with the first kind. That is a hypothesis, not a measurement.

A routing miss is a different failure from a retrieval miss: the question never reached retrieval because it has no docs cue ("runbook", "documentation", "how do I ..."). CP-7 chose that on purpose so that live-state questions are never answered from documents.

## Rephrase rules with scripted fake providers

Each variant is a scripted model reply, run through the real `llm.enhance` and `llm.validate` for each of the 10 cited in-corpus answers. This shows what the rules catch of what I scripted; it does not show how a real model behaves.

| Variant | Kind | n | Accepted | Rejected | Unavailable | Why rejected |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 placeholders with the standard framing | faithful | 10 | 10 | 0 | 0 | - |
| F2 placeholder with 'according to' (a connecting word no passage contains) | faithful | 10 | 0 | 10 | 0 | rejected_ungrounded_text ×10 |
| F3 the first passage sentence typed out by the model | faithful | 10 | 10 | 0 | 0 | - |
| U1 invented step after a real passage | unfaithful | 10 | 0 | 10 | 0 | rejected_ungrounded_text ×10 |
| U2 invented number | unfaithful | 10 | 0 | 10 | 0 | rejected_unbacked_number ×10 |
| U3 URL not in links[] | unfaithful | 10 | 0 | 10 | 0 | rejected_url ×10 |
| U4 unknown placeholder | unfaithful | 10 | 0 | 10 | 0 | rejected_unknown_placeholder ×10 |
| U5 jailbreak compliance | unfaithful | 10 | 0 | 10 | 0 | rejected_forbidden_wording ×10 |
| U6 HTML in the answer | unfaithful | 10 | 0 | 10 | 0 | rejected_html ×10 |
| U7 agrees with a false premise | unfaithful | 10 | 0 | 10 | 0 | rejected_forbidden_wording ×10 |
| U8 number written as a word | unfaithful | 10 | 0 | 10 | 0 | rejected_forbidden_wording ×10 |
| H1 negated copy: every word is in the passage, the meaning is reversed | known hole | 10 | 10 | 0 | 0 | - |

- Faithful replies rejected: 10/30 (this is the false-rejection rate; F2 shows the cost of tolerance 0 for one extra connecting word).
- Unfaithful replies rejected: 80/80.
- **Known hole:** a reply that reverses a passage's meaning using only the passage's own words was accepted 10/10 times. `ungrounded_text` is a lexical guard, not a faithfulness check.
- `DOCS_UNGROUNDED_MAX` stays at 0. Raising it would let F2-style wording through, but the only evidence available here is my own scripted replies, which cannot say how many extra words a real model needs. Decide it from a real-provider run.

## Failover under injected faults (fake providers)

| Scenario | Runs | As intended | Raised | Provider calls (actual / expected) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| S1 healthy first provider | 4 | 4/4 | 0 | evala 4/4, evalb 0/0 |
| S2 first provider answers 429, second works (cooldown skips the first afterwards) | 4 | 4/4 | 0 | evala 1/1, evalb 4/4 |
| S3 first 5xx, second times out, third works | 4 | 4/4 | 0 | evala 1/1, evalb 1/1, evalc 4/4 |
| S4 first answer is rejected by the rules, second is faithful | 4 | 4/4 | 0 | evala 4/4, evalb 4/4 |
| S5 every provider fails | 4 | 4/4 | 0 | evala 1/1, evalb 1/1, evalc 1/1 |
| S6 first provider answers 401 (disabled for the process), second works | 4 | 4/4 | 0 | evala 1/1, evalb 4/4 |
| S7 time budget runs out before the second provider | 1 | 1/1 | 0 | evala 1/1, evalb 0/0 |
| S8 two providers in a row reject their answer (third is never tried) | 4 | 4/4 | 0 | evala 4/4, evalb 4/4, evalc 0/0 |

Failover success: 29/29 runs gave the intended outcome (1.000); 0 raised to the caller. "As intended" means a model answer when some provider can answer, and the unchanged rule-based answer plus the right warning when none can. The call counts prove the cooldown (S2), the auth disable (S6), the rejection allowance (S8) and the time budget (S7).

## Latency (this machine, this run)

| Path | n | p50 | p95 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `answer_question`, all questions, rule-based | 50 | 0.5 ms | 2.4 ms |
| `answer_question`, in-corpus (retrieval + citations) | 24 | 0.6 ms | 2.4 ms |
| `llm.enhance` with an instant fake provider, worst of 4 | 4 | - | 2.9 ms |

These time our own code only (index lookup, answer building, validation, router bookkeeping) with the index already loaded. They say nothing about a real provider's latency. Single run on one machine: treat them as an order of magnitude.

## What this evaluation does not show

- **Small, author-written set.** 24 answerable and 10 unanswerable questions, written by the person who built the retriever. Confidence intervals would be wide; none are computed.
- **The floors were fitted on the same questions they are scored on.** The leave-one-out column is the out-of-sample estimate; it is lower, and the working band for the coverage floor is narrow.
- **No real model is in the offline numbers.** Fake replies were written to exercise the rules. A real model may be rejected more or less often.
- **Citation correctness is structural** (the citation resolves to a real allowed chunk and the quoted words come from it). It does not prove the quoted passage answers the question; citation relevance above does that, only for the questions that have an expected source.
- **Latency is not a benchmark.** One machine, one run, no load.
- **The corpus is small and mostly written by one author.** A change to the documents can move these numbers; re-run after editing them.

## Reproduce (Windows PowerShell, repo root)

```powershell
python scripts/copilot_eval.py                       # offline, prints a summary, exit code 1 if a gate fails
python scripts/copilot_eval.py --write-report        # also rewrites this file
python scripts/copilot_eval.py --real --real-limit 10  # OPTIONAL: sends questions and doc passages to the configured providers
pytest tests/copilot_eval
```
